verifications.claim: Ramadan in 2026 is expected to end on the evening of Thursday, March 19, or Friday, March 20, 2026.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: Support: 'Eid al-Fitr 2026 is expected to fall on the night of March 19 or March 20' (R1); 'end on March 19 or 20, or Thursday or Friday' (R5). Contradict: 'will end on the evening of Wednesday, March 18' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources support expected end around March 19-20 evening, but R6 explicitly states March 18 evening, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: Ramadan concludes with the sighting of the new crescent moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'sighting of a crescent moon signals the beginning of the next month' (R1); 'determined by the sighting of the crescent moon' (R2); 'depends on the sighting of the new crescent moon' (R3); 'contingent upon the sighting of the moon' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly state that Ramadan ends based on crescent moon sighting.

verifications.claim: The sighting of the new crescent moon marks the beginning of the festival of Eid al-Fitr.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'Shawwal... begins immediately with the sighting of the crescent moon... The first day of Shawwal brings Eid al-Fitr' (R1, R2); 'Eid al-Fitr... signals the start of Shawwal' (R3); 'Eid al-Fitr officially begins at the start of... Shawwal' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly link moon sighting to start of Shawwal and thus Eid al-Fitr.

verifications.claim: Dates are traditionally confirmed by moon-sighting committees.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'Muslims await word from Saudi Arabia' (R1); 'rely on moon spotters in Saudi Arabia' (R2); 'trained spotters in Saudi Arabia' (R7).
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe moon spotters or reliance on Saudi announcements but do not use 'committees' specifically; broader term used in claim.

verifications.claim: Most projections point to a March 19-20 completion of Ramadan in 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'expected to fall on... March 19 or March 20' (R1, R2, R5); 'expected to fall on the evening of Thursday, March 19' (R3); 'end on March 19' (R7); outlier 'March 18' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: Majority of sources project March 19-20 completion, supporting 'most projections'; minor outlier does not negate.

verifications.claim: Expected start date of Ramadan in 2026 is Feb 17 or 18, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 'began on Feb. 18' (R1); 'began on the evening on Feb. 17' (R3, R5); 'evening of Tuesday 17 February 2026' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly support expected start on Feb 17 or 18 with no contradiction.

verifications.claim: Expected end date of Ramadan in 2026 is March 19 or 20, 2026.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: Support: 'March 19 or March 20' (R1, R2, R5); 'March 19' (R3, R7). Contradict: 'evening of Wednesday, March 18' (R6).
verifications.reasoning: Most sources align with March 19 or 20, but R6 states March 18, indicating contradictory projections.

verifications.claim: Eid al-Fitr typically begins the evening of the last day of Ramadan
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 'Eid al-Fitr 2026 is expected to fall on the night of March 19 or March 20' (R1, R5); 'Ramadan will end and Eid will begin on Friday, March 20' (R2); 'expected to fall on the evening of Thursday, March 19' (R3).
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Eid starting around the evening/night coinciding with or immediately after Ramadan's end but not precisely 'evening of the last day'; broader phrasing.
